english.title: Possess article for use in connection with conversion of imitation firearms
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), not being a registered firearms dealer, you had in your possession or under your control an article, namely **(..SPECIFY THE ARTICLE..), that was capable of being used to convert an imitation firearm into a firearm intending by its use to convert an imitation firearm into a firearm
english.legislation: Contrary to section 4A of the Firearms Act 1968.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: Section 36 of the Violent Crime Reduction Act 2006 makes it an offence to manufacture, import or sell a realistic imitation firearm.

other.penalty:
Either waySummary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and / or fine.
Indictment: maximum 5 years imprisonment and / or fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2022; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 4A(1)(a)(i) of the Firearms Act 1968 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2022.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
